text:
Two men indicted on charges of assaulting and killing indie film director Kim Chang-min last year were sentenced Thursday to prison terms of 12 years and three years, respectively.
The Namyangju branch of the Uijeongbu District Court handed down a 12-year term to a 32-year-old man surnamed Lee and a three-year term to another 32-year-old surnamed Lim. The court also banned the two men from working at institutions serving people with disabilities for five to 10 years.
Lee and Lim were accused of beating Kim severely with their fists and feet at a restaurant in Guri, just east of Seoul, on Oct. 20, 2025, following a dispute over noise. Kim was taken to a hospital, where he was declared brain-dead 17 days later. He subsequently died after donating his organs to four recipients.
The defendants were also charged with violating the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities by assaulting Kim in the presence of his son who has a severe autistic disorder.
The court found Lee guilty of murder but convicted Lim only of assault resulting in death, citing insufficient evidence to establish that he conspired to commit murder.
Prosecutors requested prison terms of 20 years for Lee and 15 years for Lim in their previous hearing.
The late Kim debuted in 2016 with "Someone's Daughter" and went on to direct many socially conscious films, including "Guui Station Exit No. 3."
